scope: practice-only CelebA-HQ smile pilot: 16 original checks, 4 selected originals, seed 0
findings: Completion marker exists and final job 6221 stderr is empty. All four arms share the same four originals and seed 0; every executed scale has 60 finite steps.
OpenCLIP matches 14/16 original smile annotations: 10/10 non-smiling, 4/6 smiling. Balanced accuracy is 83.3%; this tiny practice set does not establish population accuracy.

For both jump counts the sole evaluator success is the same adding-smile edit, 4.jpg. Exact final smile margins are approximately +0.003, versus negative shortcut margins. This is one paired example, not independent evidence from two subjects.
No smile-removal edit flips OpenCLIP. The two smile-removal examples still appear smiling in every inspected grid, despite most satisfying the STEEX guide.

All four edit grids and the original-image sheet were inspected. No gross visual corruption was apparent. Exact arms have lower mean pixel L1 and weighted VGG perceptual distance than shortcut arms on this tiny sample.
Peak allocated GPU memory is at most 3.58 GiB. Mean generation time ranges from 7.53 to 14.12 seconds per explanation; image/evaluator scoring and setup are excluded.
The selected photos metadata retains guide_accuracy=0.9375 from the unfiltered 16-image practice pool; all four selected originals agree with guide, evaluator, and annotation.
recommendation: OpenCLIP is a reasonable candidate independent evaluator for a larger face experiment, with fixed prompts and checkpoint. Report adding/removing smiles separately and include continuous target-directed cosine-margin changes alongside binary success. Do not infer H2 support or general evaluator reliability from this pilot.
